newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea intervenes in forex market - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea intervenes in forex market - dealers.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea (BOK) stepped into the won/dollar interbank market on Friday, buying dollars at 891.20 won, dealers said.
The dollar rose to 892.90 after the intervention, they said.
Dealers said the central bank was seen intervening as the weakening dollar against the yen prompted the won's rise. They said the central bank wanted to slow the rise of the won.
After opening at 892.10, the won hit a high of 890.80.
BOK assistant governor Shim Hoon earlier said the dollar would stay above the current 890 won level, if the dollar/yen rate did not fall further.
"Unless the dollar/yen rate drops further from the current level, there is no reason for the dollar to fall below the 890 won mark," he said.
